brief: Goldman partner Bobby Molavi argues the flat S&P, back near its June level around 7600, is masking violent factor rotation underneath. Four forces are live simultaneously and all point the wrong way. An AI 'slow the frontier' pile-on, led by Amodei and echoed by Altman, Musk and Hassabis, is pressuring chips even as capex stays locked in and the trade shifts toward monetization proof. Oil is above $100 and drifting toward $110 after a Saudi east-west pipeline outage cut Hormuz-skirting export capacity. The 10-year yield is above 5% for the first time since 2007 against a multi-trillion-dollar T-bill refinancing wall. The Fed is odds-on to hike with inflation 140bps over target before the oil rally is priced in. Positioning is cleaner than before, which only makes the factor violence, an 11% one-day swing in the 3-month/12-month momentum pair, long-term AI winners selling off, software rallying, more visible. The note also flags a private-market AI valuation boom and unresolved Japan capital-flow questions as secondary threads.
